correctness.rationale: Every length-n output word comes from an input of length n+4, which extends to a bilateral full-shift point. Starting the subset automaton from all four-bit states recognizes exactly these words, counts them once, and makes all live states reachable. Hence a reachable Perron component gives both the correct exponential lower bound and, by finite-matrix growth, the matching upper bound. In the independent replay below, all sixteen state sets (sizes 11–14), both catalogs, all seven polynomial divisibilities and their ordered rational isolating intervals were reproduced; root counts also exclude any larger real root through 2. Exact tests on all 512 nine-bit words per code give precisely 1,3,7,8,12,14 as non-idempotent. Removing the active edge gives t^11(t−1)(t^4−t^3−t^2−t−1) in those six cases; the maximal recurrent component determines the fixed shift entropy. The fixed Perron interval lies below both B and D; the two log gaps agree with the reported approximations. Bit complement doubles every count; in the idempotent cases image equals Fix. This is a proof for one spatial image of the bilateral full shift, not merely agreement at bounded word lengths or a statement about temporal entropy.
